In this case, we have to use the identity  $1+\cot^2x =\csc^2 x.$ Rearranging this gives

$$
\eqalign{
		\cot^2 x &=\csc^2 x -1.
}
$$

Substituting this into our integral gives

$$
\eqalign{
		\int \left(5\cot^2 x -x^2\right) \, \textrm{d}x&=\int \bigg(5\left(\csc^2 x -1 \right) -x^2\bigg) \, \textrm{d}x\
				&=\int \left(5\csc^2 x -5 -x^2\right ) \, \textrm{d}x\
				&=-5\cot x -5x-\dfrac{x^3}{3}+C.	
	}
$$

First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So we can use the identity 

$$
{tan}^{2}⁡x+1={sec}^{2}⁡x\,⟹\,{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4-3{x}^{2}+4{tan}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int (4-3{x}^{2}+4({sec}^{2}⁡x-1))\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (4-3{x}^{2}+4{sec}^{2}⁡x-4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (-3{x}^{2}+4{sec}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{3}+4\operatorname{tan}⁡x+C \\  & =-{x}^{3}+4\operatorname{tan}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
